# Part A
```{r}
a <- 17
b <- 5

print(a + b)
print(a - b)
print(a * b)
print(a / b)

print(a && b)
print(a %/% b)

raise <- 2 ^ 10
```

Question #1: Run 17 / 5, 17 %% 5, and 17 %/% 5 side by side. In your own words, explain how these three results relate to each other mathematically.
```{r}
a <- 17
b <- 5 

print(a/b)
print(a%%b)
print(a%/%b)
```
Standard division gives the same decimal total, while integer division and modulo split the process into a whole-number quotient and a leftover remainder that together equal the original exact result.

Question #2: Predict the output of 10 %% 3 and 10 %/% 3 before running the code. Were you correct? If not, explain what you misunderstood.
- I am predict that running modulo will output 1 and integer division will output 3, which is correct because 3 fits into 10 three whole times with a remainder of 1 from the modulo.
